# Independent audit: exact piecewise-softmax contact allocations

Source: `candidate 7ed1287ead37cfb6`.
Full independent analytic read: **PASS. No correction identified.**
The theorem regularizes an already feasible allocation; it does not prove
new transport feasibility or a physical-body response identity.

The initial contact sets (3) are exactly the intersections of the finitely
many active-plane dominance halfspaces with C. Their finite closed union
covers each sampled fiber because its complement would contain a relative
open positive-volume subset. The moment range is compact under bounded
weak-* convergence; prescribed measurable zero sets and the sum constraint
are closed. No full-dimensionality of the row moment range is assumed.

At a relative-boundary target moment, a nonconstant relative supporting
functional exposes a PROPER face. Its nonnegative integrated score gap
vanishes exactly when every positive allocation uses pointwise maximizing
labels. Thus the face really equals the new allocation moment range, in
both directions. Its affine dimension strictly decreases. Reductions that
change only null sets cannot count as a proper step. Repeated affine scores
on a whole fiber are correctly retained as ties, not discarded as null.
This verifies finite termination and the finite hyperplane chamber claim.

On the final range, V=span(D-D) is the correct quotient. For g orthogonal
to V, the integrated allowed-score oscillation is zero, so all allowed
scores coincide almost everywhere; this proves the entire gauge invariance.
The relative ball centered at the target gives
h_D(theta)-theta.b>=r||theta|| on V. The log-sum-exp sandwich therefore
gives coercivity and attainment without a Slater assumption in the original
ambient moment space. The gradient is a difference of two attainable moment
vectors and hence lies in V; constrained stationarity puts it in V-perp,
giving exactly zero. The variance Hessian has precisely the stated gauge
kernel, proving quotient uniqueness.

The final softmax retains every original contact and all full moments.
The L moment follows from any one source-active affine plane, not an
independently imposed scalar constraint. On each chamber the affine-score
formula has a positive denominator and bounded derivatives on its compact
closure. Refining by L's affine cells gives the same local regularity for
the actual row density. For curved fibers these pieces need not be literal
polytopes; the source explicitly preserves that distinction.

The entropy identity (8) is exact: log q_i*=theta_i*.v-log Z has the same
integral against every feasible allocation because the full moments and
pointwise sum are fixed. All feasible allocations already obey the final
facial restrictions. Nonnegativity and strictness of conditional KL give
the stated unique entropy maximizer modulo null sets.

The boundary-trace argument is sound. A hyperplane cutting a convex fiber
properly meets its boundary in zero H_(d-1) measure; a supporting hyperplane
has a single interior side at its positive-area face. Finitely many walls
therefore give a unique interior chamber at surface-almost-every external
boundary point. Original contacts survive in chamber closures because they
are closed. Assigning traces on the boundary does not change mixed-volume
moments and need not coincide with an arbitrary pointwise argmax convention
on a null wall. The d=1 endpoint case is handled separately and correctly.

Finally the interval example proves a genuine obstruction to global
continuity: the prescribed upper row moment is the exact bathtub maximum,
and equality forces the upper-half indicator almost everywhere. The theorem
does not erase this jump or authorize ignoring internal interface flux under
row-specific deformations. Uniform derivative bounds over changing moment
data are also properly excluded.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
